claims.text: The material under study is a FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy.
Exposure to a high-temperature environment causes a dense oxidation film to form on the alloy surface.
The formation of the dense oxidation film requires or occurs in the presence of Al, Cr, and Si.
The dense oxidation film improves the mechanical properties of FeNiCrMn.
Formation of the oxidation film increases alloy strength.
Formation of the oxidation film improves or preserves good ductility.
FeNiCrMn without the dense oxidation film has inferior mechanical properties relative to film-bearing FeNiCrMn.
The detailed mechanism by which the oxidation film would improve mechanical properties is not fully understood.

contradictions.description: The initial material is identified only as FeNiCrMn, but the required conditions include Al and Si without specifying them as alloying additions or defining a modified composition; the stated intervention is only high-temperature exposure.

The mechanism field presents oxidation-film formation as the cause of improved mechanical properties, while the uncertainty field acknowledges that the mechanism connecting the film to those properties is not understood.
